records.title: Effects of clinostat-based microgravity simulation on the growth and differentiation of cerebral organoids using a 3D-clinostat.
records.abstract: The human brain is highly sensitive to altered gravitational environments, yet the molecular and cellular consequences of microgravity remain poorly understood due to the limited accessibility of astronaut neural tissue. Here, we employ human cerebral organoids cultured in a 3D clinostat to clinostat-based simulation and investigate neurodevelopmental responses. Organoids were exposed to continuous clinostat-based simulation for 30 days (C30), 15 days followed by 15 days of normal gravity (C15 N15), or standard gravity controls (N30). Neurochemical profiling revealed marked reductions in acetylcholine, dopamine, norepinephrine, and glutamate under microgravity, with partial recovery after re-adaptation; by contrast, GABA levels increased persistently, suggesting an excitatory-inhibitory imbalance. Transcriptomic analysis demonstrated widespread downregulation of pluripotency markers (OCT4, NANOG, SOX2), regional identity genes (FOXG1, DLX2, NKX2.1, SIX6), and neuronal differentiation markers (MAP2, DCX, VGLUT1), whereas astrocytic GFAP was robustly elevated and cortical identity marker SATB2 recovered upon re-exposure to normal gravity. Despite extensive transcriptional changes, protein levels of the neuronal marker MAP2 and the pluripotency marker SOX2 remained unchanged. Together, these findings indicate that clinostat-based simulation disrupts stemness, regional specification, and neurotransmitter balance, while promoting astrocytic lineage bias and partial recovery upon gravitational re-exposure. This study establishes human cerebral organoids as a tractable ground-based simulation model for probing brain vulnerability to space environments and for identifying candidate biomarkers and countermeasures to safeguard astronaut neurocognitive health during long-duration missions.

records.title: Digoxigenin is a Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Agent against Influenza A Virus via Degradation of Nucleoprotein.
records.abstract: Seasonal influenza A viruses (IAVs; H1N1 and H3N2) and their zoonotic variants (e.g. H5N1 and H3N8) pose persistent threats to public health, highlighting an urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. Through high-throughput screening with the constructed reporter virus H3N8-GFP, we initially identified a panel of potential antiviral agents from FDA-approved compounds. Further validation revealed that digoxigenin (Dig), the aglycone of digoxin, significantly inhibited the proliferation of H3N8, H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1 in infected primary murine alveolar epithelial cells and ESC-derived human alveolar organoids. Dig treatment protected mice from lethal challenge with H1N1 and H3N8 by increasing survival rates and reducing viral loads.Mechanistically, Dig exerts its antiviral activity by directly binding to the host Na+/K+-ATPase α1 subunit (ATP1A1), which triggers the degradation of viral nucleoprotein via both the ubiquitin-proteasome and autophagy pathways, without affecting other components of the viral ribonucleoprotein (vRNP). Our study reveals the Dig-mediated antiviral mechanism that targets the host cell degradation machinery, and identifies Dig as a promising broad-spectrum antiviral agent against IAVs.

records.title: From cortical development to glioma: neural stem and progenitor programs in tumor heterogeneity.
records.abstract: Adult gliomas are shaped by an interaction between somatic genetics and developmental cell identity rather than by either factor alone. Here, we distinguish cell-of-mutation, cell-of-origin, developmental lineage identity, and transcriptional cell state, and use this framework to compare isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant glioma with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Recent single-cell, spatial, and lineage-tracing studies show that glioma cells repeatedly co-opt neurodevelopmental programs, while genetic alterations bias, but do not fully define, the states that malignant cells occupy. Microenvironmental signals and therapy further reshape these states during tumor progression. We discuss how genetically engineered mouse models, patient-derived xenografts and tumoroids, and human organoid transplantation can test these relationships, emphasizing that complementary models and direct benchmarking to patient tissue are essential for resolving, and effectively treating, glioma heterogeneity.

records.title: Organoids as Functional Models of Hepatic Tropism in Colorectal Cancer Liver Metastasis: From a Selective Hepatic Niche to Liver-specific Vulnerabilities.
records.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) is favored by portal anatomy but determined by a sequence of organ-selective bottlenecks: sinusoidal arrest, early survival, immune escape, metabolic accommodation, and growth-pattern-specific expansion. This Review integrates direct human CRLM evidence, mechanistic models, and organoid studies to define what is established, what remains inferential, and what next-generation models must test. Paired primary-tumor and liver-metastasis organoids preserve inter- and intrapatient heterogeneity and can reproduce selected chemotherapy responses, but epithelial-only cultures cannot model hepatic receptivity. Liver-containing systems should therefore be built as question-specific modules that add hepatocytes, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, hepatic stellate cells, Kupffer or recruited myeloid cells, extracellular matrix, and flow only when required by the hypothesis. We propose an evidence-linked experimental framework combining longitudinal single-cell transcriptomics, chromatin profiling, metabolomics, isotope tracing, spatial readouts, and perturbation-rescue experiments. Particular emphasis is placed on extracellular-vesicle-mediated premetastatic niche formation, clinically observed microenvironmental evolution, and context-dependent vulnerabilities such as vessel co-option and liver-restricted immune-metabolic dependencies. We also define minimum reporting and validation standards required before organoid results can influence clinical decisions. The central conclusion is that organoids become models of hepatic tropism only when liver context is treated as a controlled causal variable rather than as the site from which tumor epithelium was sampled.

records.title: Perspectives of parents of children with monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders on research involving patient-derived neuronal models.
records.abstract: Patient-derived stem cell-based neuronal models hold great promise for advancing research into monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders (mNDDs). These neuronal models are generated using induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technologies, and are perceived as "ethically sensitive". To date, ethical discussions on the use of neuronal models have predominantly focused on three-dimensional (3D) neuronal models, such as brain organoids, while two-dimensional (2D) neuronal models - which are widely used in current research settings - remain underexplored. A better understanding of the perspectives of parents of children with mNDDs on ethical issues - including the moral status of 2D models, informed consent, autonomy, privacy and misuse - is needed. We report the results of a semi-structured interview study among parents of children with mNDDs (n = 28) investigating their perspectives on the ethically responsible use of 2D patient-derived neuronal models in research. Respondents ascribed limited intrinsic value to neuronal models, often viewing them as ethically comparable to other somatic cells. They were highly motivated to enroll their child in iPSC research, but suggested that researchers: (1) restrict the use of their child's donated material to purposes benefiting the mNDD community, (2) protect their child's privacy, (3) communicate about research findings and reuse of donated material, and (4) minimize risks and burdens of research procedures for their (vulnerable) child. Based on these findings, we provide recommendations to research groups for informed consent and engagement processes to support responsible inclusion of children with mNDDs and their families in research using iPSC-based neuronal models.

records.title: Schizophrenia heterogeneity, treatment response to clozapine, and the Johns Hopkins Schizoaffective Disorders Precision Medicine Center of Excellence.
records.abstract: Schizophrenia heterogeneity has resisted resolution for over a century, with no unifying clinical feature, biomarker, or pathogenic pathway identified. This has produced imprecise diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment, while confounding mechanistic research. Prior subtyping approaches-based on clinical phenotype, longitudinal course, age of onset, neuroimaging, physiological measures, or etiological factors-have yielded partial insights but lack established clinical utility. The Johns Hopkins Schizoaffective Disorder Precision Medicine Center of Excellence (PMCOE) brings together patients and clinicians at the Johns Hopkins Hospital and the Johns Hopkins Bayview Community Psychiatry Program with Johns Hopkins schizophrenia investigators to address this heterogeneity through stratification by treatment response, dividing patients into non-treatment-resistant (nonTRS), clozapine-responsive treatment-resistant (crTRS), and ultra-treatment-resistant (uTRS) subgroups. The term "Schizoaffective Disorder" was chosen to include schizophrenia with varying degrees of affective symptomatology, deliberately creating a broadly inclusive patient group. We hypothesize that these subtypes reflect distinct pathophysiological processes and that identifying their biological correlates will improve clinical decision-making and reveal novel therapeutic targets. The PMCOE pursues this hypothesis across four aims. Aim 1 characterizes clinical, cognitive, functional, quality-of-life, and olfactory signatures distinguishing subtypes, with preliminary data showing worse cognition and function in uTRS versus crTRS, and a temporal sequence of clozapine benefit (symptoms, then function, then quality of life). Aim 2 applies 7T structural/functional MRI-including novel measures of microvascular perfusion (iVASO) and CSF clearance (cDSC)-alongside EEG-based dynamic causal and network modeling to probe excitatory/inhibitory imbalance across subtypes. Aim 3 investigates cellular and molecular mechanisms, particularly protein homeostasis dysfunction, using patient-derived induced neurons, organoids, and extracellular vesicles, with focused study of SCHEMA-identified risk genes, including CUL1. Aim 4 leverages electronic health record data to generate validated electronic phenotypes for treatment-response subtypes and to establish a learning health system translating findings into clinical practice. By anchoring subtyping to an empirically measurable, clinically actionable outcome, the PMCOE aims to accelerate biomarker discovery for clozapine response, clarify mechanisms of treatment resistance, and transform care for individuals with schizophrenia-particularly those with ultra-treatment-resistant illness, for whom therapeutic options remain critically limited.

records.title: LeakageHunter-SCFM: Evidence-bounded dataset-lineage auditing for single-cell foundation model benchmarks.
records.abstract: To develop and evaluate LeakageHunter-SCFM, an evidence-bounded informatics framework for auditing dataset-lineage evidence and calibrating benchmark-independence claims in single-cell foundation model evaluation. LeakageHunter-SCFM extracts accessions, DOIs, URLs, and repository identifiers from manuscripts and related artifacts. The workflow canonicalizes resources, assigns dataset roles, constructs candidate overlap pairs, and applies claim ceilings before reviewer adjudication. We evaluated it in a curated development corpus, a locked retrospective external evaluation set, and a small prediction-blinded prospective proof-of-concept evaluation. The development workflow reduced 673 raw candidates to 84 filtered resource entries and 53 candidate overlap pairs. Prediction-visible reviewer forms agreed across all 140 retrospective evidence units; their historical labels yielded F1 0.842 across 132 binary-scored units. Independent prediction-blinded relabeling of all 140 units followed by third-assessor adjudication yielded precision 0.727, recall 0.667, specificity 0.910, and F1 0.696 across 136 binary-scored units. The seven-record, prediction-blinded proof of concept achieved recall 1.000 and precision 0.611 across 52 evidence units. All actionable-positive units came from one record. Restricting this analysis to full article bodies retained 50 units from five records and F1 0.759. Evidence-bounded lineage auditing supports biomedical foundation-model benchmark review by separating identifier overlap, actionable review priority, and confirmed exposure. LeakageHunter-SCFM provides a reproducible triage layer for lineage evidence and reserves claims about corpus membership and performance effects for direct supporting evidence.

records.title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
records.abstract: Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

records.title: FeDx-SF@βE assembly for AML treatment via GATA1/SLC40A1 pathway-mediated iron homeostasis disorder.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. Inducing ferroptosis in AML cells represents a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, transcriptomic analyses first revealed that ferroptosis-associated transcriptional states were closely associated with prognosis and ex vivo drug-response heterogeneity in AML, providing a rationale for ferroptosis-oriented therapeutic design. Based on these findings, and further supported by a transcriptome-based target-scoring strategy, β-elemene (βE), a clinically used natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, was selected as a candidate ferroptosis-related agent. We subsequently developed a nanodelivery system, designated FeDx-SF@βE, based on alcohol-induced silk fibroin (SF) folding to co-deliver ferric dextran (FeDx) and βE. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited a uniform particle size of 182.3 nm, favorable colloidal stability, and sustained drug release behavior. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient cellular uptake of FeDx-SF@βE by AML cells, leading to significantly inhibited cell viability. Pharmacological cell-death inhibitor rescue experiments showed that ferrostatin-1 produced the most pronounced protective effect, indicating that FeDx-SF@βE-induced AML cell death was predominantly ferroptosis-dependent. Mechanistically, βE-containing treatment suppressed the nuclear translocation of the transcription factor GATA1 and downregulated the iron efflux channel SLC40A1. GATA1/SLC40A1 gain- and loss-of-function analyses further demonstrated that activation of this axis attenuated FeDx-SF@βE-induced iron overload and ferroptotic injury, whereas suppression of this axis promoted intracellular iron retention, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage. In combination with FeDx-derived iron supply, βE-mediated inhibition of the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-export axis resulted in intracellular iron overload, glutathione depletion, ROS accumulation, extensive lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Bulk transcriptomic and virtual-cell analyses further supported the involvement of the GATA1/SLC40A1 axis in ferroptosis-associated AML states and linked βE-related transcriptional programs to this regulatory mechanism. In a disseminated AML xenograft model, FeDx-SF@βE exhibited enhanced antileukemic efficacy and favorable biosafety. Collectively, this work provides a combined ferroptosis-oriented nanotherapeutic strategy for AML treatment and highlights the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-homeostasis axis as a functionally relevant mechanism for ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicine design.

records.title: scREFINE: Label-efficient refinement of frozen scGPT embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq clustering.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) clustering remains challenging because of high dimensionality, sparsity, technical noise, and limited cell annotations. Here, we propose scREFINE, a label-efficient semi-supervised clustering framework that adapts pretrained single-cell foundation-model embeddings for accurate cell clustering. scREFINE uses a lightweight refinement head to map cells into a task-specific clustering space using only 5% labeled cells, while treating the remaining cells as unlabeled during training. To exploit information from unlabeled cells, scREFINE introduces stability-aware soft structural regularization over local neighborhoods, which leverages reliable cell-cell relations as auxiliary guidance without relying on hard pseudo-label constraints. Experiments on five benchmark scRNA-seq datasets show that scREFINE achieves the best ARI on every dataset against every baseline under an identical, leakage-free protocol (mean ± SD over four seeds). A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test over the five per-dataset means yields p=0.0625, above the conventional 0.05 threshold because only five datasets are available; we therefore interpret the consistent improvements as strong empirical evidence rather than a statistically conclusive demonstration. A common-embedding comparison confirms that these gains arise from task-specific refinement rather than the pretrained representation alone: adapted baselines receiving identical embeddings achieve 0.00-0.61 ARI, compared with 0.73-0.89 for scREFINE. Ablation analyses further demonstrate that task-specific embedding refinement is the primary driver of improvement, whereas soft structural regularization provides dataset-dependent auxiliary gains and degrades more gracefully than hard pseudo-labels when supervision is scarce. Biological marker-gene analysis confirms that the predicted clusters correspond to canonical cell populations.

records.title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network.
records.abstract: Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean R2 of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.

records.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

records.title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme.
records.abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((kcat/KM)/kw) of up to 3 x 1013 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

records.title: AlphaInterp: Revealing how AlphaFold 3 processes structure, confidence, and evolutionary information.
records.abstract: How does evolutionary information become structural knowledge? AlphaFold 3 predicts protein structures and biomolecular assemblies with remarkable accuracy, yet how it transforms comparative sequence information into three-dimensional structure remains poorly understood. Here, we use mechanistic interpretability to follow this transformation through AlphaFold 3 and identify a computational principle underlying its structural inference. By extracting single- and pair-representations across the model's forward pass and combining representational-geometry analysis, linear probing, activation patching, and perturbation of the multiple-sequence alignment (MSA) and its phylogenetic diversity, we show that AlphaFold 3 does not simply infer structure from raw sequence nor from MSA depth. Instead, a small number of sufficiently divergent homologues provides enough comparative information to largely recover the structure predicted using the full MSA. The pairformer transforms this evolutionary signal into a compact latent space in which residue-pair distances, contacts, fold similarity, and structural confidence become progressively decodable. Removing the MSA disrupts these latent geometries. Replacing it with evolutionarily similar homologues provides substantially less information, while evolutionarily unrelated sequences fail to rescue prediction despite preserving the formal alignment input. In contrast, phylogenetically diverse MSA subsampling largely restores both prediction accuracy and representational coherence. These results suggest that AlphaFold 3 has learned to infer structure by constraining its geometric priors and structural hypotheses by the sequence variation of the MSA. This framework helps explain both the model's remarkable predictive power and its characteristic failure modes, with direct implications for protein design, conformational diversity, out-of-distribution generalization, and the interpretation of model confidence.

records.title: Computational identification and comparative characterization of ligand scaffolds for VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2 kinase domains in neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
records.abstract: VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2 have distinct but complementary roles in vascular endothelial growth factor signaling, providing a rationale for comparing ligand recognition by their kinase domains in neovascular age-related macular degeneration. We integrated dual-receptor docking, fragment tree Transformer-based variational autoencoder generation, and three-dimensional Monte Carlo tree search to identify candidate ligand scaffolds. Screening 37,445 natural product-like structures retained 989 compounds, and subsequent molecular generation and physicochemical filtering produced 1,315 structures for receptor-constrained optimization. Twenty candidates were prioritized, of which VDS-1, VDS-2, and VDS-3 were examined using three independent 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations per complex and MM/PBSA analysis. VDS-1 showed the most negative MM/PBSA estimates for VEGFR-2 (-49.79 ± 0.21 kcal/mol) and VEGFR-1 (-45.95 ± 1.84 kcal/mol), whereas VDS-2 exhibited substantial between-trajectory variability. VDS-3 showed limited between-trajectory variation in its MM/PBSA estimates for both receptors, although protein-aligned ligand RMSD revealed between-replicate heterogeneity, particularly in VEGFR-1. Van der Waals interactions predominated among favorable modeled contributions, with PHE1047 in VEGFR-2 and ILE881 in VEGFR-1 emerging as recurrent interaction regions. Although VDS-1 showed favorable modeled interactions, it had substantial physicochemical and predicted safety liabilities. VDS-3 therefore represented a comparatively balanced starting scaffold for further optimization, although experimental validation and toxicity assessment remain necessary.

records.title: Reprogramming Protein Function by Expanding Chemical and Combinatorial Space: Integrating Chemical and Computational Strategies.
records.abstract: Proteins are biological macromolecules that perform critical functions, including catalysis, molecular recognition, and cellular regulation. Natural evolution has generated remarkable protein diversity, leaving vast opportunities for engineered molecular innovation. Protein engineering has evolved from the rational design of proteins over the last few decades to approaches based on directed evolution and computational methods to enhance their properties. Protein engineering is shifting from optimization-based approaches to an integrated approach, which includes rational design, directed evolution, computational and generative modeling, synthetic chemistry, synthetic biology, and laboratory automation. These strategies widen the scope of experimentally accessible chemical and structural toolboxes in proteins without sacrificing the physicochemical constraints, cellular compatibility, evolutionary processes, and experimental validation. Meanwhile, synthetic chemistry is extending the natural abilities of proteins by incorporating noncanonical amino acids, novel cofactors, and modified metal centers and catalytic environments. These technologies enable the creation of artificial enzymes, programmed molecular binders, synthetic receptors, molecular machines, and biomaterials that have functions beyond those of their natural counterparts. This review introduces advances in the protein engineering field, from past methods of modifying proteins to present-day opportunities for generating proteins with artificial intelligence, and explains how the fields of computation, chemistry, and biology are driving the future of programmable proteins.

records.title: Recent advances in fabrication strategies, functional modulation and healthcare applications of native protein-based hydrogels.
records.abstract: Native protein-based hydrogels not only possess all advantages of their denatured analogues such as exceptional biocompatibility and low toxicity, but also retain the intrinsic function of the protein building block. Therefore, they exhibit novel favorable properties including inherent bioactivity and reversible sol-gel transformation behavior. As such, they have emerged as versatile biomaterials widely used in the biomedical field. This review provides a comprehensive and up-to date overview of design strategies, formation mechanisms, and healthcare applications of native protein-based hydrogels. We systematically summarize the key cross-linking strategies for fabricating reversible native protein-based hydrogels, with particular emphasis on how these interactions govern hydrogel formation and their functionality. We highlight recent advances in fabricating these hydrogels through chemical cross-linking, physical cross-linking, metal coordination, fusion protein design, key interface redesign, de novo design, and modular design strategies, which enable precise control over hierarchical architecture, stimuli-responsiveness, and biomechanical properties. Furthermore, we explore the diverse healthcare applications of these hydrogels, with emphasis on drug delivery, wound healing, and tissue engineering. Finally, we discuss perspectives on future directions, including the integration of computational modeling, machine learning, and high-throughput experimentation to enable rational design of smart, multifunctional native protein-based hydrogels with tailored performances for next-generation biomedical applications.

records.title: Natural language-guided generation of molecular structures for single-molecule electronics.
records.abstract: As molecular science advances toward autonomous scientific discovery, enabling AI models to directly generate valid molecular structures from natural language descriptions has emerged as a critical requirement. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated the ability to map discrete chemical space into continuous semantic representation for general molecular generation, their application to single-molecule electronics (SME) remains largely unexplored. This is primarily due to the specific topological requirements of the field, such as the necessity of an anchor-backbone-anchor motif for electrode connection. In this work, we propose SingMolT5, a fine-tuned molecular LLM for natural language-guided generation of single molecules. We systematically evaluated the structural generation performance using both in-context learning (ICL) and fine-tuning strategies based on a carefully curated domain-specific instruction-tuning dataset. Results show that while ICL can capture basic molecular syntax, only the fine-tuning model can reliably enforce the anchor-backbone-anchor motif required for single-molecule measurements. More importantly, SingMolT5 achieved high structural prediction accuracy, along with strong generalization to unseen structural variations not included in the training dataset. This work provides a proof-of-concept demonstration for a text-to-structure workflow in SME, serving as a foundational step toward integrating natural language models into future autonomous workflows for single-molecule research.

records.title: Extracellular vesicle surface glycosylation in clinical chemistry: Biological mechanisms, analytical challenges, and translational evidence.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) expose a glycocalyx that integrates cellular glycosylation programs with vesicle biogenesis, trafficking and interactions in biofluids. This surface layer is analytically attractive because it can be interrogated on intact particles and can encode disease-associated changes in sialylation, fucosylation, N-glycan branching, high-mannose structures and mucin-type O-glycans. Human studies, particularly in pancreatic cancer and lung or breast cancer, have converted selected EV-associated glycan motifs into measurable liquid-biopsy signals, whereas evidence in other diseases remains preliminary. Translation remains constrained by an unresolved measurand problem: EV abundance, glycan density, carrier identity, isolation selectivity, lipoprotein contamination and affinity avidity can each change the observed signal. This review integrates the biological architecture of the EV glycocalyx with the analytical workflow required for clinical chemistry. It compares affinity, mass-spectrometric and single-EV approaches; evaluates disease-specific evidence; and defines pre-analytical, analytical and post-analytical sources of variation. A translational framework is proposed in which candidate EV glycan biomarkers progress from structural and mechanistic confirmation through intended-use assay design, analytical validation, independent clinical validation and multicenter implementation. EV glycosylation is positioned not as another untargeted omics layer but as a surface-accessible signal defined by the vesicle population and assay whose value depends on explicit definition of the vesicle population and glycan measurand.

records.title: Cytopathologic Diagnosis of Lymphomas in Serous Effusions, Cerebrospinal and Vitreous Fluid.
records.abstract: Haematolymphoid lesions in serous effusion, cerebrospinal, and vitreous fluid are encountered regularly. In the paediatric clinical setting, haematolymphoid lesions are the most common cause of malignant serous effusions. Cytologists and cytopathologists should be prepared to evaluate such samples as part of routine diagnostic practice. This article provides a comprehensive overview of the cytomorphological features and diagnostic considerations of lymphomas involving serous fluids, cerebrospinal, and vitreous fluids. B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas are most often encountered in fluid cytology specimens. A practical method for triaging lymphocyte-predominant effusions involves assessing lymphoid cell size, specifically distinguishing between small-to-medium and large lymphoid cells. A significant differential diagnosis of small-medium lymphoid cells in fluid specimens is reactive lymphocytosis while that for large cells is metastatic malignant, and atypical or malignant mesothelial cells. Cytologic evaluation of fluids containing lymphocytes provides valuable information regarding the nature of these lesions. Accurate cytologic diagnosis, with clinicopathologic correlation and judicious use of ancillary testing where possible, is essential for identifying the underlying cause of effusion, guiding therapy, monitoring disease progression or relapse, and informing prognosis. To optimize diagnostic outcomes, proper collection, transport, and preparation of fluid specimens is required. Collaboration with haematopathologists and use of standardized cytologic reporting systems further contribute to diagnostic accuracy and consistency. Emerging technologies, including molecular profiling, liquid biopsy, single-cell multi-omics and artificial intelligence, offer promising avenues for advancing the diagnosis and prognostication of haematolymphoid malignancies in fluid-based samples. Further research will determine their clinical utility.

records.title: Diagnostic value of tumor-educated platelet transcriptomics in cancer: a systematic review of technical considerations and diagnostic accuracy.
records.abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and the search for noninvasive markers for cancer screening and diagnosis, as well as for patient monitoring, is of utmost importance to better and earlier detect cancer. As the second most abundant cell type in the bloodstream, platelets interact bidirectionally with cancer cells, acquiring cancer-associated molecular alterations that modify their transcriptomic profile and give rise to so-called tumor-educated platelets (TEPs). As an easily accessible and abundant blood component, TEPs have emerged as a promising liquid biopsy source for cancer diagnostic biomarkers. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the clinical utility of the TEP transcriptome as a potential source of diagnostic biomarkers in solid and hematological neoplasias. It also identifies the major challenges and future perspectives for their clinical implementation. The review protocol was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO: CRD42024486960).

records.title: Early Detection of Ovarian Cancer: Current Strategies and Future Directions.
records.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a major cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, mainly because most cases are diagnosed at advanced stages due to non-specific early symptoms. Although early detection is essential for improving clinical outcomes, accurate and accessible screening remains a major challenge, owing to the non-specific nature of early symptoms, the pronounced histological and molecular heterogeneity of the disease, and the poor performance of conventional screening approaches based on cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) and imaging modalities. This review outlines the major biological and technical challenges in the early diagnosis of OC, briefly summarizes the value and limitations of conventional diagnostic approaches and focuses on current progress in emerging biomarkers, including circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA)/cell-free DNA (cfDNA) alterations, exosomal biomarkers and mesothelin multi-marker combined detection strategies, and novel technologies, such as artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, single-cell sequencing and biosensors for early detection. We also discuss the advantages, current limitations, practical considerations and translational barriers of these approaches. Future advances in OC screening will require the integration of sensitive biomarkers, multimodal detection strategies and more accessible, cost-effective technologies to improve early diagnosis and patient survival.

records.title: From recognition to delivery: nucleic acid aptamers in miRNA-related diagnosis and therapy of hepatocellular carcinoma.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the most common primary malignant liver tumour, remains a major clinical challenge because of its low early diagnosis rate and high post-treatment recurrence. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) play key regulatory roles in HCC development and progression and are potential liquid biopsy biomarkers and therapeutic targets. However, the low abundance and instability of miRNAs in body fluids, together with the limitations of conventional detection methods, have hindered their clinical translation. Nucleic acid aptamers, owing to their high affinity, specificity, and ease of chemical modification, are valuable in miRNA-related detection and targeted delivery. This narrative review summarises technical strategies for aptamer-based and aptamer-inspired detection of HCC-associated miRNAs, as well as aptamer-guided miRNA delivery systems in HCC therapy. Importantly, most aptamers used in HCC research do not directly bind miRNAs; instead, they target HCC cells, surface proteins, or exosomes, whereas miRNAs serve as detection analytes or therapeutic cargo. It analyses the design logic and potential integration pathways of "recognition-delivery" platforms, while distinguishing conceptual integration from experimentally validated single-platform systems. Challenges and future directions are also discussed.

records.title: Elevated serum KIF20A in hepatocellular carcinoma: exploring its potential as a circulating biomarker.
records.abstract: To evaluate serum KIF20A expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and assess its association with HCC status using a bioinformatics-guided clinical RT-qPCR approach. This cross-sectional study included 110 participants: 50 with HCC, 10 with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection without HCC, and 50 healthy controls. Serum hsa-miR-5192, HSPA1B, LPH02229A/CRHR1-IT1, and KIF20A were quantified by RT-qPCR as relative quantification (RQ). Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) was the conventional comparator. Secondary analyses evaluated AFP with KIF20A using logistic regression, AUC comparison, and repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation. KIF20A showed significant overall differential expression (P=0.003), with higher expression in HCC than in healthy controls (P=0.007) and the HCV non-HCC group (P=0.004). Median KIF20A RQ was 2.95 in HCC, 0.40 in healthy controls, and 0.255 in HCV. For HCC versus all non-HCC participants, KIF20A remained associated with HCC after accounting for AFP (OR 2.10 per 1-SD increase in log-transformed KIF20A; 95% CI 1.01-4.37; P=0.048), but the combined model did not materially improve discrimination over AFP alone (AUC 0.968 vs 0.964; DeLong P=0.606). Serum KIF20A showed HCC-associated upregulation and retained an exploratory association with HCC after accounting for AFP. However, it did not provide meaningful incremental discrimination beyond AFP; the small disease-control group and absence of external validation preclude claims of HCC specificity or clinical diagnostic readiness.
